newsitem.title: PERU: Peru opposition slams Fujimori plan on pol parties.
newsitem.headline: Peru opposition slams Fujimori plan on pol parties.

text.p: The Peruvian opposition on Thursday charged that President Alberto Fujimori's plan to increase the number of political parties was a election maneuver aimed at softening the government's authoritarian image.

Members of the opposition said Fujimori's announcement in Germany on Wednesday that he would halve the number of signatures required to form a political party was an attempt to create a smokescreen for a possible bid by the president for an unprecedented third term in office.
The government has so far rejected opposition party calls for a referendum on a congressional interpretation of the constitution allowing Fujimori to stand in the 2000 election.

"It's nothing more than a distracting maneuver...so that the government's attempts to thwart a referendum are forgotten," said Antero Flores-Araoz, a congressmen from the opposition Popular Christian Party.
Peruvian constitutional analyst Fernando Tuesta said Fujimori had made the announcement abroad to maximize the impact of a measure that could make his government look less authoritarian.

Since coming to power in 1990, Fujimori has stabilized the economy and made Peru attractive to foreign investors. But his authoritarian style --particularly his dissolving of Congress in 1992 and creation of a substitute legislature the next year -- has led to criticism that the government restricts democratic institutions.
